scope: Great Pyramid of Giza (Khufu), simplified schematic
title: Great Pyramid of Giza
blurb: The tomb of Pharaoh Khufu, built around 2560 BC, in simplified schematic form: the 146.6 m pyramid over its 230.4 m base, the Grand Gallery and the granite King’s Chamber within, and the funerary complex in outline. The Sphinx belongs to Khafre’s complex and is not modeled.

systems.name: Pyramid mass
systems.description: The stepped masonry core and the white Tura limestone casing, shown as built, rising 146.6 m over a 230.4 m square base.

systems.name: Entrance
systems.description: The original entrance on the north face and its chevron gable blocks.

systems.name: Passages
systems.description: The descending and ascending passages, the 47 m Grand Gallery, the antechamber and the well shaft.

systems.name: Chambers
systems.description: The King’s Chamber of red Aswan granite with its sarcophagus, the relieving chambers, the Queen’s Chamber and the subterranean chamber.

systems.name: Modern discoveries
systems.description: Voids found by the ScanPyramids project: the Big Void of 2017 and the north-face corridor of 2023.

systems.name: Funerary complex
systems.description: The mortuary temple, causeway and valley temple in outline; the valley temple was never excavated.

systems.name: Bedrock platform
systems.description: The leveled bedrock of the Giza plateau on which the pyramid stands.

explanations.core courses (lower): The lower stepped courses of the pyramid core, built of roughly horizontal masonry totaling about 2.3 million blocks averaging 2.5 tonnes. Course count and setback are schematic.
explanations.core courses (middle): The middle stepped courses of the pyramid core. Course count and setback are schematic.
explanations.core courses (upper): The upper stepped courses of the pyramid core. Course count and setback are schematic.
explanations.core courses (apex): The topmost stepped courses of the pyramid core, below the capstone. Course count and setback are schematic.
explanations.north casing: The north face of the pyramid as built, sheathed in fine white Tura limestone up to 2.5 m thick, loosened by a 1301 earthquake and carted away in 1356 to build mosques and fortresses in Cairo. Shown complete as built.
explanations.south casing: The south face of the pyramid as built, sheathed in fine white Tura limestone. Shown complete as built.
explanations.east casing: The east face of the pyramid as built, sheathed in fine white Tura limestone. Shown complete as built.
explanations.west casing: The west face of the pyramid as built, sheathed in fine white Tura limestone. Shown complete as built.
explanations.surviving casing stones: Casing stones still in place around the base of the pyramid, showing the original precision fit.
explanations.pyramidion capstone: The capstone that crowned the pyramid at 146.6 m, long since lost. Exact shape is schematic.
explanations.entrance and chevron blocks: The original entrance on the north face, with massive chevron gable blocks spreading the load above it. Entrance height above the base is schematic.
explanations.descending passage: The descending corridor at about 26.5 degrees: one branch continues down to the subterranean chamber, the other turns up the ascending passage. Exact routing is schematic.
explanations.ascending passage: The ascending passage rises at 26 degrees for 39 m to the Grand Gallery, about 1.05 m wide and 1.2 m high. Exact routing is schematic.
explanations.grand gallery: The Grand Gallery: a corbelled passage 47 m long and 8.5 m high, rising at 26 degrees, with seven stepped tiers and ramps with notches on both sides.
explanations.antechamber and portcullis slabs: The small antechamber before the King’s Chamber, with granite slabs that slid down to seal the tomb after the burial. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.well shaft: The narrow, near-vertical shaft connecting the lower descending passage with the bottom of the Grand Gallery, likely an escape route for the workers who sealed the tomb. Exact routing is schematic.
explanations.king’s chamber walls: The walls of the King’s Chamber, 10.47 by 5.23 m, built entirely of red granite from Aswan, some 900 km south, carrying work-gang graffiti naming Khufu.
explanations.king’s chamber floor: The floor of the King’s Chamber, about 42.99 m above the base of the pyramid.
explanations.king’s chamber roof slabs: The nine flat granite slabs forming the ceiling of the King’s Chamber, each weighing 25 to 40 tonnes.
explanations.khufu’s sarcophagus: The sarcophagus of Khufu, hollowed from a single piece of red Aswan granite, placed during construction; found lidless and empty, with no lid ever found.
explanations.relieving chambers: Five rough chambers stacked above the King’s Chamber, the top one with a pointed gabled roof, spreading the weight of the masonry above. Shown as solid schematic masses.
explanations.king’s chamber air shafts: The narrow air shafts of the King’s Chamber, about 20 cm square, the northern about 59.5 m and the southern about 53.5 m long, reaching the outer faces. Exact routing is schematic.
explanations.queen’s chamber: The Queen’s Chamber, about 5.74 by 5.23 m with a gabled roof; despite its name, archaeologists believe it was not meant for a queen. Exact layout is schematic.
explanations.queen’s chamber shafts: The two narrow shafts of the Queen’s Chamber, about 20 cm wide, which do not reach the surface and are blocked by limestone stones. Exact routing is schematic.
explanations.subterranean chamber: The subterranean chamber, the largest of the three chambers but totally unfinished, rough-cut in the bedrock about 27 m below the plateau surface. Shown as a solid schematic mass.
explanations.big void (scanpyramids, 2017): The Big Void found by the ScanPyramids muon tomography survey in 2017: a cavity about 30 m long above the Grand Gallery. Its purpose is unknown; it has never been entered. Rendered as a schematic mass.
explanations.north-face corridor (2023): A 9 m long, 2 by 2 m corridor behind the chevron blocks above the entrance, confirmed by endoscopy in 2023. Exact interior geometry is schematic.
explanations.mortuary temple: The mortuary temple at the east foot of the pyramid, 52.2 m north to south and 40 m east to west, nearly gone except for black basalt paving. Exact plan is schematic.
explanations.causeway (outline, partial): The causeway that linked the mortuary temple with the valley temple near the Nile. Shown in outline at a partial, schematic length.
explanations.valley temple (unexcavated, outline): The Valley Temple, buried beneath the village of Nazlet el-Samman; basalt paving and limestone walls have been found, but the site has not been excavated. Rendered in outline at a schematic position.
explanations.leveled bedrock platform: The leveled bedrock of the Giza plateau on which the pyramid stands. Exact extent is schematic.
